title: Isaiah Chapter 63 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 63 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 63 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 63.

questions.question: Who is described as coming from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah?
options: A mighty savior speaking in righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: A mighty savior speaking in righteousness
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:1 identifies the figure as one who speaks in righteousness and is mighty to save, coming from Edom with dyed garments from Bozrah.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63, why are the garments described as red like someone who has trodden in the winefat?
options: Because the garments are dyed red
Because the person has trodden the winepress alone, staining the garments with blood
Because of the glory of the apparel
Because of the strength of the traveler
questions.correctAnswer: Because the person has trodden the winepress alone, staining the garments with blood
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:3 explains that the figure trod the winepress alone and their blood stained the garments, causing the redness like someone who has trodden in the winefat.

questions.question: What has the speaker declared is in his heart, and what has come according to Isaiah 63?
options: The day of vengeance and the year of redemption
The day of peace and the year of blessing
The day of mourning and the year of sorrow
The day of judgment and the year of punishment
questions.correctAnswer: The day of vengeance and the year of redemption
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:4 states, 'For the day of vengeance is in mine heart, and the year of my redeemed is come.'

questions.question: What did the speaker notice about help and support in Isaiah 63?
options: There was none to help and none to uphold
questions.correctAnswer: There was none to help and none to uphold
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:5 says, 'And I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63, what did the speaker’s own arm do?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:5 states that 'mine own arm brought salvation unto me.'

questions.question: How will the speaker deal with the people according to Isaiah 63?
options: Tread them down in anger and make them drunk in fury
questions.correctAnswer: Tread them down in anger and make them drunk in fury
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:6 says, 'And I will tread down the people in mine anger, and make them drunk in my fury.'

questions.question: What will the speaker mention according to Isaiah 63?
options: The lovingkindnesses and praises of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The lovingkindnesses and praises of the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:7 says, 'I will mention the lovingkindnesses of the LORD, and the praises of the LORD.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 63 says the speaker trod the winepress with many people helping him.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:3 states, 'I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the people there was none with me.'

questions.question: True or False: In Isaiah 63, the speaker says the day of vengeance is in his heart.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:4 says, 'For the day of vengeance is in mine heart.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 63 states that the speaker’s fury upheld him when there was no one to help.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:5 says, 'therefore mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 63 describes the garments as clean and untouched by blood.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:3 explains that the blood of the trodden people was sprinkled upon the garments, staining all the raiment.

questions.question: In Isaiah 63, what comes first: the speaker mentions the LORD's mercies or declares the day of vengeance is in his heart?
options: Declares the day of vengeance is in his heart
questions.correctAnswer: Declares the day of vengeance is in his heart
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:4 declares the day of vengeance is in the speaker's heart before Isaiah 63:7 where the LORD's mercies are mentioned.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63, what does the speaker say about the strength of the people?
options: He will bring their strength down to the earth
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring their strength down to the earth
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:6 says the speaker will 'bring down their strength to the earth.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63, the speaker says he will mention the praises of the LORD according to what?
options: All that the LORD hath bestowed on us
questions.correctAnswer: All that the LORD hath bestowed on us
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:7 states, 'I will mention the praises of the LORD, according to all that the LORD hath bestowed on us.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63, from where is the person coming who is glorious in apparel and mighty to save?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:1 says, 'Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?'

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 63 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 63 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:8, how does God describe His people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:8 states that God said, 'Surely they are my people, children that will not lie,' indicating His view of His people as honest and faithful. This connects with verse 9 where He acts as their Savior.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:9 say about God's response to the affliction of His people?
options: He was afflicted with them and saved them through the angel of His presence
He abandoned them to suffer alone
questions.correctAnswer: He was afflicted with them and saved them through the angel of His presence
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:9 explains that 'In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them,' showing God's empathy and active salvation. This is linked to verse 8 where He calls them His people.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 63:10 describe the people's relationship with God's Spirit?
options: They rebelled and vexed His holy Spirit, causing God to become their enemy
They faithfully followed the Spirit's guidance
They were indifferent to the Spirit
They fully embraced the Spirit without rebellion
questions.correctAnswer: They rebelled and vexed His holy Spirit, causing God to become their enemy
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states the people's rebellion and vexing of God's holy Spirit, resulting in God turning to be their enemy, reinforcing the seriousness of disobedience seen in verse 9's affliction context.

questions.question: What question does God ask about Moses and His people in Isaiah 63:11?
options: Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock?
Who will lead them into battle?
Why have they forgotten the law?
When will they return to the promised land?
questions.correctAnswer: Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:11 recalls God's past deliverance by asking 'Where is he that brought them up out of the sea with the shepherd of his flock?' linking back to Moses and God's guidance, which contrasts with their current state in verse 10.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:12, how did God lead His people through the sea?
options: By the right hand of Moses with His glorious arm, dividing the water
By sending a pillar of cloud only
By parting the Red Sea with Moses' staff alone
By leading them through the desert without water
questions.correctAnswer: By the right hand of Moses with His glorious arm, dividing the water
questions.explanation: Verse 12 describes God leading the people by Moses' right hand with His glorious arm, dividing the water to make an everlasting name, demonstrating His power in salvation as remembered in verse 11.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 63:13 illustrate God's guidance through difficult terrain?
options: He led them through the deep like a horse in the wilderness so they would not stumble
He left them to find their own way
He caused them to stumble as a test
He led them only by day, not by night
questions.correctAnswer: He led them through the deep like a horse in the wilderness so they would not stumble
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:13 says God led His people 'through the deep, as an horse in the wilderness, that they should not stumble,' emphasizing His careful guidance through challenges, connected to verses 11-12 about His deliverance.

questions.question: What comparison is made in Isaiah 63:14 regarding God's leading of His people?
options: As a beast going down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest
As a warrior fighting battles alone
As a shepherd neglecting his sheep
As a king ignoring his subjects
questions.correctAnswer: As a beast going down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest
questions.explanation: Verse 14 compares God's leading to a beast resting in the valley, showing gentle care by the Spirit, linking to God's purpose to make Himself a glorious name, echoing His guidance in previous verses.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 63:15, what does the speaker ask God to reveal about His character?
options: His zeal, strength, compassion, and mercies
questions.correctAnswer: His zeal, strength, compassion, and mercies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:15 implores God to look down from heaven and reveal His zeal, strength, and mercies, reflecting a plea for God's active compassion as previously displayed in verses 8-14.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:16 say about God's relationship to His people despite their ancestral ignorance?
options: God is their Father and Redeemer, even if Abraham and Israel are ignorant of them
God has abandoned them because of their sins
God only acknowledges their ancestors, not them
God's name is temporary and changing
questions.correctAnswer: God is their Father and Redeemer, even if Abraham and Israel are ignorant of them
questions.explanation: Verse 16 affirms God as Father and Redeemer to His people regardless of Abraham or Israel's recognition, highlighting God's unchanging role, which contrasts with the people's rebellion in verse 10.

questions.question: In Isaiah 63:17, what request is made to God concerning His people?
options: Return for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: Return for the sake of Your servants, the tribes of Your inheritance
questions.explanation: Verse 17 asks God why He has made the people stray and hardened their hearts, then pleads for His return for the sake of His servants, connecting to the theme of restored relationship found in earlier verses.

questions.question: What condition does Isaiah 63:18 describe about the possession of the holy land?
options: The people have possessed it only a little while, and adversaries have trodden down the sanctuary
The people have full and uncontested possession
The adversaries have been completely defeated
The sanctuary has been rebuilt and glorified
questions.correctAnswer: The people have possessed it only a little while, and adversaries have trodden down the sanctuary
questions.explanation: Verse 18 laments that the people of holiness have held the land briefly and that enemies have trampled the sanctuary, illustrating a loss connected to their disobedience noted in verses 10 and 17.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:19, what is said about God's rule over adversaries?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:19 says, 'We are thine: thou never barest rule over them; they were not called by thy name,' indicating God never ruled over the adversaries, so the correct answer is true.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 63:11 depicts God forgetting His past deliverance of Israel.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:11 shows God remembering the days of old with Moses and His people, recalling His mighty acts of deliverance, so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 63:10 teaches that rebellion against God’s Spirit results in God becoming an enemy and fighting against His people.
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states that because the people rebelled and vexed the holy Spirit, God turned to be their enemy and fought against them, confirming the truth of this statement.

questions.question: How does the passage in Isaiah 63:8-9 teach about God’s faithfulness in times of suffering?
options: God shares in their affliction and saves them through His presence and love
God ignores their suffering and lets them perish
God punishes the faithful more severely
God only rewards the strong and prosperous
questions.correctAnswer: God shares in their affliction and saves them through His presence and love
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 emphasize God's empathy ('In all their affliction he was afflicted') and active salvation ('the angel of his presence saved them'), teaching believers to trust God's faithfulness during hardship.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 63 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 63.

questions.question: In Isaiah 63:15, what is being asked to 'look down from heaven' and behold?
options: The zeal and strength of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The zeal and strength of the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:15 calls on God to look down from heaven and behold His zeal and strength, the sounding of His bowels (compassion) and mercies toward the speaker.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:16, what title is given to the LORD, emphasizing His eternal nature?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:16 refers to the LORD as 'our father, our redeemer,' and notes that His name is from everlasting, highlighting His eternal and paternal role.

questions.question: What complaint is made to the LORD in Isaiah 63:17 regarding the people's spiritual condition?
options: They have hardened their heart and erred from His ways
They have become rich and forgotten Him
They have built idols and false temples
They have fled to foreign lands
questions.correctAnswer: They have hardened their heart and erred from His ways
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:17 questions why the LORD has made them err from His ways and hardened their heart from His fear, implying a lament over their spiritual rebellion.

questions.question: In Isaiah 63:18, what has happened to the sanctuary of the LORD?
options: It has been trodden down by adversaries
It has been rebuilt and glorified
It has been hidden from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It has been trodden down by adversaries
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:18 laments that the adversaries have trodden down the sanctuary, indicating desecration and loss of holy possession.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'We are thine' in Isaiah 63:19?
options: It affirms the people's identity as God's own despite hardships
It declares the people's independence from God
It expresses the people's rejection of God's rule
It announces a new covenant with foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms the people's identity as God's own despite hardships
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:19 asserts 'We are thine,' confessing the people's belonging to God even though God never ruled over their adversaries or called them by His name.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage also speaks of God as 'our father' and 'redeemer,' echoing Isaiah 63:16?
questions.explanation: Malachi 2:10 also refers to God as 'our Father' and emphasizes the covenant relationship, echoing Isaiah 63:16’s depiction of God as father and redeemer.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 63:3 where God says, 'I have trodden the winepress alone'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:3 uses metaphor, comparing God's judgment and vengeance to treading a winepress alone, symbolizing His wrath and justice.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:9, who is described as saving the afflicted people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:9 states that 'the angel of his presence' saved the afflicted, showing God's intimate involvement in delivering His people.

questions.question: What is the reason given in Isaiah 63:10 for God turning to be the enemy of His people?
options: They rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: They rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:10 explains that the people's rebellion and vexing of God's holy Spirit caused Him to turn against them and fight against them.

questions.question: In Isaiah 63:12, what miraculous event is recalled that demonstrated God's power through Moses?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:12 recalls God leading the people by Moses' right hand, dividing the water before them to make Himself an everlasting name, referring to the Red Sea crossing.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 63:19 suggests that the people of God were never called by God's name.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:19 says 'they were not called by thy name' referring to the adversaries, not the people of God, so it is false that God's people were never called by His name.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'year of my redeemed is come' in Isaiah 63:4 indicates a time of salvation and restoration.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:4 speaks of 'the year of my redeemed is come,' signaling God's intended time of deliverance and restoration for His people.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's vengeance and salvation portrayed in Isaiah 63:4?
questions.explanation: Romans 12:19 speaks about vengeance belonging to God, which echoes the theme of divine vengeance and salvation in Isaiah 63:4.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'redeemed' in Isaiah 63:4 and 63:9, and what does it imply about God's relationship with Israel?
options: To buy back or rescue, implying God's saving acts
To create anew, implying God's creative power
questions.correctAnswer: To buy back or rescue, implying God's saving acts
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'redeemed' (ga'al) means to buy back or rescue, indicating God's active role in saving Israel from bondage or oppression as in Isaiah 63:4 and 63:9.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 63:14 use a simile to describe God's care for His people?
options: Like a beast going down into the valley, God causes His people to rest
Like a lion roaring, God defends His people
Like a river flowing, God nourishes His people
Like a shepherd calling, God gathers His people
questions.correctAnswer: Like a beast going down into the valley, God causes His people to rest
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:14 uses the simile of a beast going down into the valley to illustrate how the Spirit of the LORD caused the people to rest, showing God's provision and care.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 63 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 63 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:1 indicate about the character of the figure coming from Edom?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:1 describes the figure as 'glorious in his apparel,' indicating majesty and strength.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:3, what will happen to the people due to the speaker's anger?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:3 states that the speaker will 'tread them in mine anger,' indicating judgment and punishment.

questions.question: In Isaiah 63:4, what does the speaker express regarding the 'day of vengeance'?
options: It is a day of joy
It is a time of peace
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:4 reveals that 'the day of vengeance is in mine heart,' showing a deep emotional response to injustice.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:8 reveal about the relationship between the LORD and His people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:8 states, 'Surely they are my people,' affirming the covenant relationship between God and Israel.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Isaiah 63:9 regarding His response to Israel's affliction?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:9 explains that 'in all their affliction he was afflicted,' demonstrating God's compassion and mercy.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 63:10, what was the result of the people's rebellion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:10 states that their rebellion caused the LORD to 'be turned to be their enemy,' indicating divine judgment.

questions.question: What significant event does Isaiah 63:11 recall in relation to Moses?
options: The parting of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: The parting of the Red Sea
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:11 recalls the deliverance from Egypt, emphasizing God's historical acts of salvation through Moses.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 63:14 describe the guidance provided by the Spirit of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:14 illustrates that the Spirit of the LORD led His people to make 'thyself a glorious name,' highlighting divine guidance.

questions.question: What plea does Isaiah 63:15 make regarding the LORD's attributes?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:15 asks where the LORD's 'mercies toward me' are, pleading for the recognition of God's compassion.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:16 affirm about the LORD's identity?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:16 states, 'Doubtless thou art our father,' emphasizing the intimate relationship between God and His people.

questions.question: What is the theme of the lamentation found in Isaiah 63:17?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:17 expresses a lament about being made to err and the hardening of hearts, indicating deep sorrow.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:18 suggest about the duration of Israel's possession of the land?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:18 notes that 'the people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while,' indicating a temporary situation.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 63:19 reveal about Israel's identity and relationship with the LORD?
options: They are called by His name
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:19 states, 'We are thine: thou never barest rule over them,' reaffirming their identity as God's chosen people.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Isaiah 63:5 and 63:6 convey about God's intervention?
options: He brings salvation through His own strength
He ignores the plight of His people
questions.correctAnswer: He brings salvation through His own strength
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:5 states that 'mine own arm brought salvation' and verse 6 speaks of God's anger, showing His active intervention.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight is drawn from Isaiah 63:9 and 63:10 regarding God's nature?
options: God requires human effort for salvation
questions.explanation: Isaiah 63:10 reveals that due to rebellion, God became their enemy, indicating a serious consequence for unrepentant sin.
